finding.claim: Unauthenticated SSRF and local file read primitive: file_get_contents() is called on a fully attacker-controlled URL. It accepts http(s), ftp, and file://, php://, and similar wrappers. The response is only returned as a length, so the SSRF is semi-blind. It still allows internal port and host probing, cloud metadata access (response size acts as an oracle), and file-existence/size probing.

trace.note: POST request with 'feed' parameter enters the branch; no auth check
$_POST['feed'] passed directly to file_get_contents as URL/path
strlen of the fetched body echoed back, giving a size oracle

finding.guards_checked: No require_admin() call on this path (it is defined at line 4 but only used at line 18). No scheme or host allowlist, no private IP / metadata IP blocklist, no DNS resolution pinning, and no redirect restrictions. Only the session_start() on line 2, which does not enforce authentication.

verdict.reason: import.php:11-13 passes $_POST['feed'] straight into file_get_contents() and echoes strlen of the result; require_admin() (defined at line 4) is only called at line 18, so the sink has no auth check, allowlist, or scheme/host validation.

finding.claim: SSRF via the webhook URL: curl_init() and curl_exec() fetch an attacker-supplied URL with no scheme, host, or IP validation. Requires an admin session, so this is lower severity. curl accepts gopher://, file://, and similar schemes by default, and follows no restrictions on internal targets. The request is semi-blind (the body is not returned), but it can reach internal services and metadata endpoints.

trace.note: curl_exec issues the request to the attacker-chosen target

finding.guards_checked: require_admin() session check is present at line 18, which limits exposure to admins (or anyone who can obtain or forge an admin session, or CSRF an admin since there is no CSRF token). No URL scheme or host allowlist, no CURLOPT_PROTOCOLS restriction, no private-IP blocking.

verdict.guard_found: require_admin() session check at import.php:18 (auth gate only). There is no URL, scheme or host validation and no CURLOPT_PROTOCOLS restriction.
verdict.reason: The trace matches import.php:17-22, but the sink at import.php:20-22 is reachable only after require_admin() at import.php:18 passes (import.php:5 requires $_SESSION['is_admin']). The source is therefore admin-only and not controllable by an unauthenticated or low-privilege attacker. A CSRF route against an admin is plausible, since no token is checked, but that is not shown in the code.
